parsed.reason: The clause "Takes the late afternoon now" is a plain, true third-person observation about what the time change means. The event moved earlier (from 6:30 to 4:15-5:00 p.m.), freeing up the late afternoon—exactly the thing a friend would remark on naturally. It avoids restatement (doesn't repeat the times), doesn't address the reader, contains no count language, and fits the same-day rescheduling context. Short, direct, worth the room.
